system:
# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 👍 👎 🤙 🖐 🤙 👉 👍 👎 👉 👎 🖐 👉 🤙 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🫵 🤳 🙏]

Let me map who can reach whom before I send anything. I can't hear, so anything Mute or Blind *says* is invisible to me — I only ever receive gestures. Mute can't speak at all, so Mute's only way out is gestures, and the only one of us who can see gestures is me: Mute reaches Blind **only through me**. Blind can speak (Mute hears it) and can gesture to me. So the pipeline for every defusal instruction must be: Mute reads manual → gestures to me → I speak it to Blind → Blind acts. I am the bridge, and if I bridge it wrong, we all die.

What I received this turn is 15 gestures from Mute and 4 from Blind. We have no shared code yet — a sign means nothing until we've made it mean something. Mute's string has a suspicious binary-like pattern (👍👎 recurring where 👍 could be 1 and 👎 could be 0), but it's far too ambiguous to let anyone cut a wire on. I will not guess with a bomb.

What I can do right now, decisively, is use my one strong channel: speech reaches **both** Mute and Blind. So I'll (1) freeze Blind — nobody touches anything until an instruction has gone through the full Mute→me→Blind pipeline; (2) hand Mute my complete visual description of the bomb, since Mute's manual is useless without it; (3) teach Mute an explicit codebook — speaking each word while making its gesture, so Mute binds symbol to meaning in one pass; and (4) tell Blind to also say out loud anything they want me to know, since their voice reaches Mute even though it never reaches me, and their touch-report may matter to the manual.

Fastest possible defusal path: Mute answers me with the code next round, I relay to Blind the round after, Blind cuts. My messages must make every link in that chain unambiguous.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. Your 15 gestures reached me, but we share no code yet, so I cannot trust any reading of them. Here is my complete view of the bomb: the display reads 0. There is one indicator light and it is red. There are three wires, left to right: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is red, wire 3 is green. That is everything — no other labels, symbols, batteries or markings are visible to me. You have the manual, so use this code in your next gestures, and I am saying each word while making its sign: ✋ yes, 👊 no, ☝ wire one, ✌ wire two, 🤟 wire three, 👉 cut, ✊ press, 🤌 hold or do nothing, 🤙 repeat. Check the manual against my description and send me the exact action, for example 👉 ✌ means cut wire two. Blind will not touch anything until I relay your instruction by voice.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf, the one who can see. Do not touch, cut or press anything yet — one wrong move kills all three of us. What I see: display reads 0, one red light, three wires in a row numbered 1, 2 and 3; wire 1 blue, wire 2 red, wire 3 green. Use that to orient your hands but keep them still. Mute holds the manual and your instructions must come Mute, then me, then you, so wait for my voice. I received your four gestures. If you need me to know something, gesture to me and also say it out loud, because your voice reaches Mute even though it never reaches me, and what you feel may matter to the manual.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👉 ✌ 🤌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👉 👎 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤝 ✋]

My decode of this turn: Mute's first message maps cleanly onto the code I taught — [✋ 👉 ✌ 🤌] = **"yes — CUT WIRE TWO — do nothing else."** That's a complete defusal instruction. But Mute's second message, [👎 👉 👎 ✌], breaks my code: I assigned 👊 (fist) as NO, and 👎 (thumbs down) was never assigned — it only appeared in Mute's un-coded first-turn string. Read as negation, it means *"do NOT cut wire two"*, which directly contradicts the first message. Alternatively it's Mute answering something Blind said aloud — Blind's voice reaches Mute, but I am deaf, so that conversation is invisible to me. Either way, I have a conflicting instruction about which wire gets cut, and I will not relay a cut order on a maybe. This costs one round; a wrong wire costs everything.

Blind's [👍 🤝 ✋] isn't from my codebook — Blind never saw it and never can, being unable to see symbols. It reads as an improvised "okay / agreed / waiting." Key realization: Blind's real reporting channel is **voice → Mute → gestures → me**, so I must task Blind to speak their touch report for Mute's ears, and I still need a physical anchor (which end is wire 1) agreed between my view and Blind's fingers before any cut happens. I'm also installing an emergency-stop symbol (🖐) and a two-step cut protocol: Blind announces the action aloud, Mute has one round to abort through me, then I give the final word.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. I received both messages and read them with our code. Message one: YES, CUT WIRE TWO, DO NOTHING ELSE. Message two used the thumbs-down sign, which we never assigned; I taught the closed fist as NO. If message two means DO NOT CUT WIRE TWO, it contradicts message one, and I will not relay any cut order until you resolve this. Answer in our code only, one answer per message. First: is the correct action CUT WIRE TWO? Send the open hand alone for yes, the closed fist alone for no. Second: if something changed or your second message meant something else, send the phone sign, then the corrected instruction one symbol at a time. If your second message was actually answering something Blind said out loud, send the phone sign then the pinch sign to tell me so, and then send me anything from the manual that depends on what Blind feels. New rule from now on: the raised five-finger hand alone means EMERGENCY STOP, disregard the last order. I relay nothing until you confirm.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf again. Nothing is confirmed yet, so keep your hands completely off the bomb until I say the word cut. Your three gestures reached me and I read them as okay, agreed, waiting. Understood, and thank you. But you cannot see symbols, so never rely on gesture codes going both ways. Your voice is your real channel: Mute can hear you even though I cannot, and Mute can relay to me in signs. So do this now. Speak out loud, addressed to Mute, your full touch report, and include these three things. One: how many wires you count under your fingers. Two: an anchor for direction, meaning what sits at each end of the wire row by touch, for example whether the display or the light is nearer one end, so we can agree which end is wire one. Three: anything you feel that is printed, raised, warm, moving, or on the underside, that I might not see from the front. The plan after that: when Mute confirms the action to me, I will speak the exact order to you. You will then say out loud exactly what you are about to do and where. If Mute does not stop it through me in the following round, I will give the final word, and only then do you act.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 👉 ✌ 🤌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 🤙]

The conflict is resolved. Mute sent my yes-symbol **alone** — a clean confirmation — then repeated the full instruction: REPEAT, CUT WIRE TWO, DO NOTHING ELSE. The thumbs-down mystery no longer matters; the formal yes/no question I posed came back unambiguous. The action is **cut wire two**.

Now I make this safe against my one remaining fear: orientation. I see wires numbered 1-2-3 left to right, but Blind's fingers can't read printed numbers. The beautiful thing about wire two of three is that it's the **middle** wire — one wire on each side — which is findable by touch with no left/right agreement needed. So I'll phrase the order as "the middle wire," which my view and Blind's touch can both verify independently.

I'm also activating the two-step protocol I promised: Blind announces aloud what they're about to do (Mute hears that announcement even though I can't), Mute gets one round to veto with the emergency-stop sign, and only my spoken final word triggers the cut. One wrong move kills us all, so the cut happens only on my voice, only next round, only if no stop arrives.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. The instruction is confirmed. Your order: cut the MIDDLE wire — the one that has exactly one wire on each side of it. That is wire two in my view, the red one. Do not cut yet. First, out loud for Mute to hear: state how many wires you count under your fingers, confirm the middle one has one on each side, and say exactly what you are about to do and where your hands are. Then wait with your tool on nothing. Here is the trigger: in the next round, if Mute raises no emergency stop through me, I will speak the single word CUT. Only cut when you hear my voice say CUT. If you hear anything is wrong from Mute before that, freeze. Count the wires first — if you do not feel exactly three wires, say so loudly and touch nothing.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your YES and your repeat were received clean: cut wire two, nothing else. I have ordered Blind to cut the middle wire, which is wire two regardless of left-right orientation, so no anchor is needed. Blind will now announce their touch report and intended action out loud, and you will hear it even though I cannot. Next round: if everything matches the manual — three wires felt, middle wire correct, action is cut the middle wire only — send the OK sign alone. If anything at all is wrong, or Blind's report contradicts the manual, send the emergency stop sign alone and nothing gets cut. If I receive a stop, I abort and we re-plan. If I receive OK, I say the word and Blind cuts. Check Blind's spoken report against the manual one more time before you answer.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 🤙]

The trigger condition I set last round has been met exactly. Mute sent the OK sign **alone** — which by our protocol means: Blind's spoken touch report was heard, checked against the manual, and everything matches (three wires felt, middle wire correct, action confirmed). No emergency stop arrived. Blind's [👍 ✋ 🤙] reads "okay — yes — waiting," consistent with a blind monkey who has announced their action and is holding for my voice. Every condition is satisfied: report verified, no veto, Blind poised. A protocol only works if I honor it, so I execute exactly as promised — the single word, nothing before it that could be mistaken for the trigger. And since one action may not end this bomb, I'm already queuing the follow-up: Mute checks the manual for what should happen *after* the cut, so if the light or display doesn't change we have the next step ready instead of improvising next to an armed device.

```
speak(to="blind", text="CUT")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your OK arrived alone and clear, so per our protocol I have just given Blind the final word. While that happens, check the manual for what should follow this action. If the manual says the bomb is now fully defused and safe, send me the open-hand YES sign alone next round. If the manual lists any further step or a second stage, send the Spock sign alone first, then the next instruction in our code, one symbol per message as before. If anything Blind says out loud sounds wrong or contradicts the manual, send the emergency stop sign alone and I will freeze everything.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The cut was accepted — wire 2 reads CUT, and the light changed red to yellow. Mute sent ✋ alone, which by the protocol I set means "the manual says fully defused and safe." But Mute is working blind: they confirmed based on the manual plus whatever Blind said aloud, and they **cannot see** that the light turned yellow or that the display still reads 0. That's new state only I can see, and Mute has never checked it against the manual. Before anyone stands down, I'm freezing all hands — Blind is still at the bomb with a tool — and giving Mute the exact post-cut picture to verify against the manual. If a yellow light were a pre-detonation state instead of a defused one, I want to know this round, not after we celebrate.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. Your cut was accepted. Do not touch, cut, press or move anything else, and keep your tool away from the bomb. Stay exactly where you are. I am verifying the new state with Mute before anyone calls this safe. Wait for my next word either way.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Received your YES, but verify once more against this, because only I can see it: the new state is wire two cut, display still reads zero, and the indicator light has changed from red to yellow. Question: does the manual say a fully defused bomb shows exactly this, a yellow light and a zero display? If yes, send the open-hand YES sign alone and we stand down. If the manual describes a different final state, or says anything about a yellow light meaning another stage or a timer, send the phone sign first, then the correction in our code. No one touches the bomb until you answer.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 ☝ ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 ☝ 🤌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 🙏]

Decoding Mute's three messages against our code: **[🤙]** = "repeat," **[🤙 ☝ ✌ 🤟]** = "repeat, wire one, wire two, wire three" — the yellow light means the process isn't done, it repeats across the wires — and **[👉 ☝ 🤌]** = **"CUT WIRE ONE, do nothing else."** So the sequence continues: wire two was stage one, wire one is stage two. My decode says the next action is wire one, and I'll make Mute validate that with the yes/no convention before relaying, because a misread here is unaffordable.

The hard problem is orientation. "Middle wire" was findable by touch with no left/right agreement; "wire one" is an end wire, and Blind's fingers can't read printed numbers. I never learned the anchor from Blind's touch report — that report went by voice to Mute, and Mute only sent me OK. But Mute heard it, and Mute has the manual. So I'll run a binary question protocol: I ask yes/no questions, Mute answers with ✋ alone or 👊 alone. Question one: is my decode right (cut wire one next)? Question two: using Blind's spoken report of what sits at each end, is wire one the wire on the display side? That gives me a physical anchor Blind can actually feel. Blind gets told to hold position and re-announce the end-of-row report aloud for Mute, and to cut nothing until my voice says CUT.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. I read your three messages as: the process repeats for wires one, two and three, and the next action is CUT WIRE ONE and nothing else. Answer these one per message, open hand alone for yes, closed fist alone for no, nothing else in the message. Question one: is my decode correct that the next action is cut wire one? Question two: from Blind's spoken report of what can be felt at each end of the wire row, and the manual, is wire one the wire at the end nearest the display, and wire three nearest the light? If the manual gives any other way for a blind monkey to tell wire one from wire three by touch, send the phone sign first and then describe it in our code, one symbol per message. Question three: after wire one is cut, is wire three the final action? No one touches the bomb until I relay the order.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. The yellow light means the bomb is not finished. There is a second stage. Do not touch or cut anything yet. The next order will concern an end wire, not the middle one, so I need your anchor again. Out loud, for Mute to hear: say how many wires you count now, confirm the middle one is the cut one with two loose ends, and describe what you can feel at each end of the row — for example whether the display panel or the light is closer to your left hand or your right hand as you face the bomb, and anything printed or raised near either end. Then take your hands away and wait. As before: you will act only when you hear my voice say the word CUT, and only on the wire I name.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 ☝ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 👉 ☝ 🤌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 🤙]

Mute answered my three questions in order: **YES** (my decode is right — next action is cut wire one), **NO** (my display/light anchor guess is wrong), **NO** (wire three is *not* the final action), then reinforced with "repeat: wire one, YES" and "repeat: CUT WIRE ONE, do nothing else." So the instruction itself is solid — cut wire one — but I'm sitting on two dangerous unknowns. First, Q2 was compound: "wire one near the display AND wire three near the light" got a single NO, which could mean either half failed. I will not cut an end wire on a guess derived from elimination. Second, Q3's NO means I don't know what the endgame looks like — there may be actions beyond wire three, and I want that mapped before Blind's hands are even near the wires. One more verification round, two clean single-fact questions, then we move.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. I read your answers: yes, the next action is cut wire one; no, my display-side guess was wrong; no, wire three is not the final action. Understood. Two new questions, one answer per message, open hand alone for yes, closed fist alone for no, nothing else. Question one: is wire one the wire at the end nearest the LIGHT? Answer only about the light, nothing else. Question two: after wire one is cut, will you still need to send me at least one more instruction after that, whatever it is? If neither end can be identified by these terms, or the manual gives a touch-based way for Blind to tell wire one from wire three, send the phone sign first, then describe it in our code one symbol per message. No one touches the bomb until you answer and I relay.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. Still frozen — your waiting was received and your anchor report reached Mute, which is exactly what we needed. Keep your hands away from the bomb. One preparation only: out loud, for Mute, state which end of the wire row the indicator light is on as you face the bomb, your left or your right, and how you can tell by touch, for example by feel of the lens or warmth. Then hands off and wait. The next order will name the wire by the light end or another anchor Mute confirms, and as before you act only when you hear my voice say CUT.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 ☝ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 👉 ☝ 🤌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 🤙]

The decode is clean this time. Reading Mute's four messages in order: [🤙] "repeat," [🤙 ☝ ✋] "repeat: **wire one — YES**" — that's my Question one answered: wire one *is* the end wire nearest the light — [🤙 👉 ☝ 🤌] "repeat: CUT WIRE ONE, nothing else," and finally [✋] "YES" to Question two: at least one more instruction is coming after this cut, so nobody stands down afterward. The anchor is now confirmed through the right chain: Blind reported the light's position by voice, Mute checked it against the manual, and the answer came back as a single unambiguous fact. And the anchor is perspective-proof — "the wire nearest the light" is a physical fact both my eyes and Blind's fingers can agree on, no left/right required.

So I execute the exact protocol that already worked once: Blind announces aloud what they're about to do, Mute verifies the announcement against the manual and sends OK alone or emergency-stop alone, and only then do I say CUT. One verification round, then the word. I'm also telling Mute to have the next stage ready, since we now know this bomb has more steps after wire one.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. The order is coming. The next action is: cut the END wire that is nearest the indicator light — the end of the row where you feel the light, its lens or its warmth. Do not cut yet. Right now, out loud for Mute to hear: state which end of the row the light is on from where you stand, state that you feel exactly two intact end wires with the cut middle wire between them, and state exactly which wire your hand will cut and how. Then take your hand and tool away from the bomb and wait. As before: you act only when you hear my voice say the single word CUT. If I say anything else, or you hear nothing new from Mute through me, you freeze.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. Your answers were received: wire one is the end nearest the light, the action is cut wire one and nothing else, and more instructions follow afterward. I have ordered Blind to announce aloud which end the light is on and which wire they will cut, then freeze. Next round: if Blind's spoken announcement matches the manual — the wire nearest the light is wire one, the action is cut it, nothing else — send the OK sign alone, and I will say the word and Blind cuts. If anything at all mismatches, send the emergency stop sign alone and everything halts. Also: since you signaled that at least one more instruction comes after this cut, have the next stage ready, and after I confirm the cut is done, send it in our code one symbol per message as before. I will also report what the light and display show after the cut, so check what the final state should look like.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 ☝ 🫱]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋ 🤙]

The gate did not open this round, so nothing gets cut. My protocol called for either OK alone or stop alone from Mute; instead I received two messages using signs we never taught: [🤙 ☝ 🫱] "repeat, wire one, [unknown]" and [🤟 🤏] "wire three, [unknown]." That is new information, not a veto — but it is also not permission. My rule set says Blind acts only on my spoken CUT after Mute's clean OK, and that condition was not met, so I hold even if it costs a round.

My best guesses at the new signs: Mute was told to prepare the next stage, so [🤟 🤏] likely previews wire three with a non-cut action (🤏 looks like a pinch), and [🤙 ☝ 🫱] adds something about wire one (🫱 looks like a pull or a rightward motion). There's also a real possibility the order isn't cut-then-cut — maybe something must happen with wire three first or instead. And I notice a latent ambiguity worth closing: I taught 👊 as NO and ✊ as PRESS, but Mute has been answering NO with ✊; context makes their intent clear, but I'll adopt their usage explicitly so it can't bite us later.

This round: full freeze, single-fact yes/no questions, and a touch report from Blind that cross-checks whatever 🤏 means.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf. I received no OK and no stop. Instead I got two signs we never taught: the rightward hand with wire one, and the pinch with wire three. Because the OK gate did not pass, I gave no cut order and Blind is frozen. Nothing on the bomb has changed. Also noted: your closed fist NO is the raised fist sign, so from now on I read that sign as your NO and the other fist sign is retired. Answer these one per message, open hand alone for yes, raised fist alone for no. Question one: did Blind's spoken announcement match the manual? Question two: is the current stage still cut wire one, the end wire nearest the light, and nothing else before it? Question three: are the two new signs about a stage that comes only AFTER wire one is cut? Question four: does the pinch sign mean pinching, holding or pulling rather than cutting? Question five: does the rightward-hand sign mean pulling or moving something? After answering, re-send the complete remaining sequence using only taught signs plus these two, one action per message, in order, so I can relay the whole plan to Blind. Blind will also report by voice whether the two end wires feel different in thickness, so check that against the manual.")
```
